title: Workspace owns adding, removing and pruning panes
body:
Adding a named pane is written at three sites: `Workspace::add_tab`, `new_terminal_pane` and the fallback arm of `commit` in `compositor.rs`. Each runs `unique_pane_name`, then `add_transient` or `Layout::new`, sets `cwd`, and calls `router.add_pane`. Removing one is written at `remove_pane` and `finish_closing_tab`; each calls `router.remove_pane` and `agents.remove`, and only `remove_pane` clears `scratch` (the bug "Closing a tab that holds the scratch pane leaves the workspace naming a pane that is gone").

The rule "an empty pane stays only while it is pinned or is the scratch pane" is written at four sites, `close_pane`, `toggle_pin`, `toggle_scratch` and `toplevel_destroyed`, each with its own mix of `matches!(kind, Transient)`, `clients.is_empty()` and `scratch_pane() == Some(name)`. That name comparison appears at about nine sites across `compositor.rs` and `panes.rs`. Inside `close_pane`, the arms `(None, Transient)` and `(None, Anchor { .. }) if scratched` have identical bodies.

`commit` and `show_tab` also write `pane.clients` and `pane.shown` from outside `panes.rs`, while `step_tab` and `remove_client` keep the invariant that `shown` points at a client.

## Proposal

- `Workspace::add_pane(tab, base, cwd) -> (id, name)` and `Workspace::forget_pane(name)` that clears router, agents and scratch.
- `Workspace::is_scratch(&Pane)`, `Pane::pinned()` and one `Workspace::prune_if_empty(tab, id)` that every site calls after its own change.
- `Pane::add_client(client)`, which knows where a terminal tab goes, and `Pane::show(index)`, so `clients` and `shown` are written only in `panes.rs`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/913b1d2c
notes.text:
What landed in bf80ab9, against the proposal:

- `Workspace::add_pane(tab, base, cwd) -> id` as proposed. It returns only the id, since neither caller used the name. `add_tab` keeps its own code, since it builds a new `Layout` rather than splitting one.
- `Workspace::forget_pane` was already in place from c577da4, so removal needed no change.
- The rule became `Workspace::keeps_empty(&Pane)` plus `State::prune(workspace, tab, id)`. `prune` stays on `State` because removing a pane also relayouts, refocuses and finishes closing tabs, which reach viewers and clients.
- `close_pane` keeps its own test. Closing an empty pane removes it unless it is pinned and not the scratch pane, which is not the prune rule: an empty scratch pane goes when closed by hand.
- `toplevel_destroyed` still compares `scratch.pane` with the pane's name by field, because it holds the pane mutably there.
- No `Pane::pinned()` method: `pinned` is already a plain field since 99e533a.

The `State` fields the decade-003057 note left here (`workspaces`, `next_workspace`, `unplaced`, `sidebar_open`) stay plain fields. `unplaced` is a list of toplevels waiting for a pane and `sidebar_open` is a frame setting, so they do not belong with the workspace list. A struct around `workspaces` and `next_workspace` would take only `add_workspace` and `workspace_index` off `State`, and both also start children and listeners.
